description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of entity types identified in a biomedical named entity recognition (NER) task, likely from the study “From Zero to Hero: Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts.” The chart is divided into 24 distinct categories, each representing a different biomedical entity type, with percentages indicating their relative frequency. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to “Protein” entities, which constitute 32% of the total. The second largest, in orange, is “DNA” at 15%. Other notable categories include “Chemical Family” (6%), “Disease” (5%), “Cell Type” (5%), and “Drug” (4%). Several categories such as “Frequency,” “Cell Line,” and “Dosage” each account for 3%, while “Strength,” “Gene Or Gene Product,” and “Form” each represent 2%. The remaining categories — “Specific Disease,” “Reason,” “Route,” “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Modifier,” “RNA,” “Disease Class,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” “ADE,” and “Composite Mention” — each occupy 1% or less, with some visually indistinguishable due to their small size. The chart uses a diverse color palette to differentiate segments, and percentages are labeled directly on the slices for clarity. The overall distribution suggests a strong emphasis on molecular entities (Protein, DNA) in the dataset, with progressively smaller contributions from more granular or contextual biomedical concepts.
